problem.text: Conversion and output compilation retained cached native Safetensors handles across successive module reads. The loader opens multiple FILE handles per source file, so retaining collections also retains those resources.

reasoning.text: Release file resources at module boundaries rather than discard the collection: close() clears cached handles but preserves headers and tensor-to-file mappings, allowing later reads to reopen files.

impact.text: This should reduce accumulated open-file pressure, at the cost of reopening files shared by successive modules. It does not change quantization calculations or output shard allocation.

source_notes.text: Issue #33, “Error converting model,” reports compilation failing at qtensors_stc.get_tensors with “Too many open files (errno=24).” Its connection to this change is inferred from that exact matching call site and the new adjacent close(); the supplied discussion does not explicitly link the commit.

Issue #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” concerns Cholesky factorization during quantization. Issue #21, “Build Failure on Windows: CUDA 12.4 / PyTorch 2.7.0+cu126 / VS 2022,” concerns extension compilation and was closed without a reported solution. Neither discussion establishes a file-handle failure addressed by this patch.

limitations: No conversion, native-loader execution, descriptor-count measurement or performance test was run. Successful completion of the reported failing job is unverified.
The change concerns resource lifetime rather than numerical arithmetic; a standalone scalar computation would not establish native file closure or runtime resource limits.

chapters.title: Release source handles after module reads

claims.text: In conversion main(), the new module.config.stc.close() runs after loading each unquantized module or slice and reporting alternate-key clones, before calibration capture and quantization. It therefore also runs for modules without quantization targets.

In compile_model(), each module's tensors are read from the working qtensors collection, made contiguous and retained in file_dict before the collection is closed. The shard is saved afterward: closing handles does not clear the tensors accumulated for serialization.

The default immediate native loader reads into allocated tensor storage rather than a file-backed mapping. Its close routine calls fclose on every cached native handle and also frees existing pinned staging buffers. The Python loading alternative already scopes each file with a context manager.
The additions are normal-path cleanup points, not try/finally guards. They shorten retention between successful module reads without adding exception-path cleanup.

annotation.summary: Closes cached Safetensors handles after each conversion module load and each compilation module read, reducing resource retention while preserving loaded tensors and reusable collection metadata.
